issues.reason: The rejected alternative is a NON-FINITE clause, which the instruction set explicitly keeps out of the sealing route ("sealing is finite-clause-only") and instead reifies at top level with no tense/status of its own, a shape it states "asserts or denies nothing about occurrence" (control infinitives, causative complements, the purpose infinitive "to check the drain") — so the three atoms claim no hundred-year rabbit life, and the rejection itself is recorded by the surface connective atom `(RatherThan sk_live_2 sk_live_1)`.

gaps_confirmed: preferential / substitutive "rather than <non-finite clause>, <clause>": the connective inventory licenses only cause / purpose / concession / contrast heads, and no construction marks one reified eventuality as the dispreferred alternative to another
new_gaps: predicative capacity "as a N" ("live one day as a tiger") — the preposition-named oblique's object rule mints a witness for an article-marked NP, but a non-referential capacity phrase arguably wants the bare kind constant the parser used; the instruction set does not say which
an imperative whose adjunct clause is not itself commanded: the `Directive` seal covers only the commanded eventuality, leaving the adjunct outside the seal with no stated treatment
notes: The commanded clause is correctly sealed under `Directive` with no tense and no minted addressee, and the durations are the licensed `(Measure e duration <n> <unit>)` form. `RatherThan` follows the multiword-connective CamelCase convention but its preferential sense sits outside the four licensed connective senses — recorded as the gap, not charged as a defect.
